blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Running import and export operations at this level means owning the handoffs between a small number of roles: the exporter who packs and documents the goods, the carrier that moves them, the customs broker who handles the paperwork at each border, and the importer who receives and pays. Each role is clear in the textbook, but in real operations, the gaps between roles are where most problems live.

The manager's job is to make those gaps invisible. When the carrier arrives, the paperwork is ready. When the documents reach customs, the values and codes match the physical goods exactly. When the shipment is released, the importer is already expecting it.

Operations that run on clean handoffs feel almost boring. Operations that live in the gaps feel exciting — and lose money on every other container.

items.q: According to the text, where do most problems in operations live?
items.why: "the gaps between roles are where most problems live."

items.q: What is described as the manager's job?
options: To make the gaps between roles invisible
To personally pack and document the goods
To reduce the number of containers shipped
items.why: "The manager's job is to make those gaps invisible."

items.q: When the documents reach customs, what should be true?
options: The importer should have already paid in full
The values and codes should match the physical goods exactly
The carrier should still be en route
The exporter should renegotiate the price
items.why: "the values and codes match the physical goods exactly."

items.q: The author suggests that an operation which feels "exciting" is most likely…
options: Ready for a new market launch
Losing money because of poor handoffs
items.why: Inferência: o texto contrapõe "boring" (limpo, lucrativo) a "exciting" (vive nas lacunas e perde dinheiro).

items.q: Which statement would the author most likely DISAGREE with?
options: Clean handoffs make an operation predictable.
Documents must match the physical goods.
The roles themselves are usually the hardest part to get right.
items.why: Inferência: para o autor, os papéis são claros; a dificuldade está nas passagens entre eles, não dentro de cada papel.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Charlotte apresentando o novo checklist de handoff à equipe. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Right, let's start with what actually happened. Over the last month we had three shipments that lost nine days between them — and not one of those delays was a customs problem. Every single one sat in the gap between us and the carrier, or between us and the broker.

So I've redrawn the handoff checklist, and there is one rule behind all of it: every gap now has a named owner. If the packing list has to reach the broker before the truck arrives, someone's name is against that line. Not "the team" — a person.

The broker whose file is cleanest clears fastest, every time. That's not luck. It means the codes and the values match the goods before anything crosses a border. So from now on, we check that here, on our side, not at the frontier.

I know a checklist feels dull. But dull is exactly what we're aiming for. The exciting shipments are the ones that cost us money. Let's make the next quarter completely boring.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: How many days did the three shipments lose between them?
items.why: "three shipments that lost nine days between them."

items.q: According to Charlotte, where did the delays actually happen?
options: At customs, because of paperwork errors
In the gap between her team and the carrier or broker
items.why: "Every single one sat in the gap between us and the carrier, or between us and the broker."

items.q: What is the single rule behind the new checklist?
options: Nothing ships without the manager's signature
Every gap now has a named owner
The broker checks everything at the border
items.why: "every gap now has a named owner… Not 'the team' — a person."

items.q: When Charlotte says the codes and values should be checked "here, on our side, not at the frontier," she implies that…
options: Catching errors before the border avoids costly delays
The border is the best place to catch errors
The broker should stop checking the file
items.why: Inferência: verificar antes de cruzar a fronteira evita que o problema apareça tarde, quando já custa dias.

items.q: What does Charlotte mean by wanting the next quarter to be "completely boring"?
options: She wants to cut the checklist entirely
She wants the team to work fewer hours
She wants smooth operations with no costly surprises
items.why: Inferência: "boring" para ela é sinônimo de operação limpa e previsível; "exciting" é o que custa dinheiro.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "Every handoff between two teams needs a clear owner." A handoff is…
options: the point where responsibility passes from one party to another
items.why: Handoff = passagem: o momento em que a responsabilidade passa de um para o outro.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "The ___ handles all the paperwork at each border so the goods can cross legally."
items.why: Customs broker = despachante, responsável pela documentação nas fronteiras.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Once customs clears the shipment, the officer will ___ the goods to the importer."
items.why: To release = liberar; é o verbo usado quando a alfândega solta a mercadoria.

items.q: "There was a gap between our records and the carrier's." A gap here is…
options: an empty space or mismatch where things fail to connect
items.why: Gap = lacuna: o vão entre as partes onde as coisas deixam de se encaixar.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "If the HS ___ on the invoice does not match the product, customs will stop the shipment."
items.why: Code = código; a fatura precisa trazer o código correto da mercadoria.

blocks.instruction: Expressões e phrasal verbs comuns em operações de importação e exportação. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The broker still has to sign off on the declaration before it goes to customs." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "We will roll out the new checklist to all three shipping lanes next week." To roll out means to…
items.why: Roll out = implantar de forma progressiva.

items.q: "The carrier pushed back on the earlier pickup time." This means the carrier…
items.why: Push back on = resistir, contestar — sem necessariamente recusar de vez.

items.q: "The team agreed on the fix but never followed through." They…
options: asked the broker to do it
failed to carry it out to the end
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi combinado; aqui não fizeram.

items.q: "If a container is held, we need to sort out the mismatch before it clears." To sort out means to…
items.why: Sort out = resolver, acertar o problema.
